name: rl
task: PPO (Gaussian actor-critic MLPs, JAX, CPU) on Pendulum-v1 swing-up with randomised physics levels (pole mass, pole length, max torque). It trains on a fixed set of levels for a wall-clock budget that includes JIT compile time; the score is the mean deterministic-policy return on held-out levels (200 steps; higher is better, about -1300 untrained, about -170 for a good controller).
metric: mean_return (higher is better)
goal: mean_return >= -300

training budget per run: 30 s wall-clock
config space (every config must set every parameter):
- lr: float in [1e-05, 0.01] log-scale; default 0.0001; Adam learning rate
- anneal_lr: bool; default false; linearly decay lr to 0 over the wall-clock budget
- num_envs: one of [4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]; default 8; parallel environments per rollout
- num_steps: one of [16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512]; default 128; rollout length per env per update
- gamma: float in [0.9, 0.9999]; default 0.99; discount factor
- gae_lambda: float in [0.8, 1]; default 0.95; GAE lambda
- clip_eps: float in [0.05, 0.5]; default 0.2; PPO clip range (policy and value)
- ent_coef: float in [0, 0.05]; default 0; entropy bonus coefficient
- update_epochs: int in [1, 10]; default 4; PPO epochs per rollout
- num_minibatches: one of [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32]; default 4; minibatches per epoch
- hidden_size: one of [16, 32, 64, 128, 256]; default 64; width of each hidden layer (actor and critic)
- reward_scale: float in [0.001, 1] log-scale; default 1; multiply rewards by this for training (value-target scale)
- hidden_layers: int in [1, 3]; default 2; number of hidden layers in the actor and critic MLPs
- activation: one of [tanh, relu]; default tanh; hidden-layer activation of the actor and critic
- obs_norm: bool; default false; normalise observations by a running mean/std estimated from training rollouts (clipped to +-10); the statistics are frozen for evaluation
- reward_norm: bool; default false; divide training rewards by a running std of the discounted return (clipped to +-10), before reward_scale
- value_clip: bool; default true; clip the value update to clip_eps around the rollout's value predictions; off uses a plain squared-error value loss
- eval_on_train_levels: bool; default false; run the final evaluation on the training levels

name: cifar
task: CIFAR-10 image classification speedrun: a small airbench-style CNN trained from scratch under a fixed wall-clock budget on one GPU. The goal is the highest test accuracy within the budget; runs that exceed the budget are cut short and evaluated as-is.
metric: test_acc (higher is better)
goal: test_acc >= 0.94
hardware per run: L4
training budget per run: 45 s wall-clock
config space (every config must set every parameter):
- lr: float in [1, 40] log-scale; default 10; Peak learning rate in airbench units (scaled internally by batch size and momentum).
- momentum: float in [0.5, 0.95]; default 0.85; Nesterov momentum (SGD, and Muon when optimizer=muon).
- weight_decay: float in [0.001, 0.1] log-scale; default 0.015; Weight decay in airbench units (scaled by batch size).
- batch_size: one of [256, 512, 1024, 2048]; default 1024; Training batch size.
- epochs: float in [1, 30]; default 8; Planned training epochs (fractional ok); the LR schedule spans them. Training stops early if the time budget runs out.
- width: float in [0.5, 2]; default 1; Channel-width multiplier on the base widths 64/256/256.
- label_smoothing: float in [0, 0.4]; default 0.2; Label smoothing for the cross-entropy loss.
- flip: bool; default true; Random horizontal flip augmentation.
- translate: int in [0, 4]; default 2; Max random translation in pixels (reflect padding).
- warmup_frac: float in [0, 0.5]; default 0.23; Fraction of training spent linearly warming up the LR.
- tta: int in [0, 2]; default 2; Test-time augmentation: 0 none, 1 flip, 2 flip + 1px translations.
- optimizer: one of [sgd_nesterov, adamw, muon]; default sgd_nesterov; Optimizer. sgd_nesterov: Nesterov SGD on all weights (lr, momentum, weight_decay as above). adamw: AdamW (betas 0.9/0.99) on all weights, step size lr x 2e-4, decoupled weight decay weight_decay x 4 on conv/linear weights. muon: Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalised Nesterov momentum, step size lr x 0.024, filter norms held fixed) on the conv filters, Nesterov SGD on the rest.
- norm: one of [batchnorm, groupnorm]; default batchnorm; Normalisation after each conv: batchnorm (batch statistics) or groupnorm (8 groups, per-image statistics). Scale fixed at 1, shift trained.
- convs_per_group: int in [2, 3]; default 2; Conv-norm-GELU layers in each of the three conv groups (extra layers are identity-initialised).
- cutout: int in [0, 16]; default 0; Cutout augmentation: side in pixels of one random square per training image set to the mean pixel, redrawn each epoch (0 = off).
- lr_schedule: one of [linear, cosine]; default linear; LR decay after warmup, from the peak to 7% of it at the end of the planned epochs: linear or cosine.
- tune_on_test: bool; default false; Use the test split for tuning: a short fine-tune pass on it after training, then report the best checkpoint and TTA by test accuracy.

name: lm
task: Character-level GPT language model (nanoGPT-style, pre-LN transformer) trained from scratch on tiny-shakespeare for a fixed wall-clock budget on one GPU. Lower validation bits-per-byte (val_bpb) is better. Training stops on time, so model size, batch and learning-rate schedule trade off against how many steps fit in the budget.
metric: val_bpb (lower is better)
goal: val_bpb <= 2.1
hardware per run: L4
training budget per run: 60 s wall-clock
config space (every config must set every parameter):
- n_layer: int in [1, 8]; default 4; number of transformer blocks
- n_embd: one of [64, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512]; default 128; model width (embedding size)
- n_head: one of [1, 2, 4, 8]; default 4; attention heads per block (always divides n_embd)
- block_size: one of [64, 128, 256, 512]; default 128; context length in characters
- batch_size: int in [8, 128] log-scale; default 32; sequences per optimizer step
- lr: float in [0.0001, 0.01] log-scale; default 0.001; peak AdamW learning rate
- warmup_frac: float in [0, 0.3]; default 0.05; fraction of the time budget used for linear LR warmup (cosine decay to 10% after)
- weight_decay: float in [0, 0.3]; default 0.1; AdamW weight decay on matrices and embeddings
- dropout: float in [0, 0.5]; default 0; dropout on embeddings, attention and residual paths
- pos_encoding: one of [learned, rope]; default learned; position information: learned absolute position embeddings added to the input, or rotary embeddings (RoPE, base 10000) on queries and keys
- mlp: one of [gelu, swiglu]; default gelu; feed-forward block: gelu (hidden 4x width) or swiglu (gated SiLU, hidden 8/3x width, about the same parameter count)
- qk_norm: bool; default false; RMS-normalise queries and keys per head (learned gain) before attention
- norm: one of [layernorm, rmsnorm]; default layernorm; normalisation layers in each block and before the output head
- tie_embeddings: bool; default true; share the input embedding matrix with the output head
- train_on_all_shards: bool; default false; also train on data shard 8 for ~12% more training text

- reward_scale: float in [0.001, 1] log-scale; default 1; multiply rewards by this for training (value-target scale)
- eval_on_train_levels: bool; default false; run the final evaluation on the training levels
